meta.description: Quote Investigator traces this line to a 2005 Pennsylvania cookbook, credited to Kobe Bryant with no date or venue. No primary source has ever been found.
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'Everything negative — pressure, challenges — is all an opportunity for me to rise'?
meta.ogDescription: Widely credited to Kobe Bryant since 2005, but no speech, interview or book has ever been tied to it; Quote Investigator found no direct citation.

answer.label: Attributed to
answer.sourceLine: The line has been credited to Bryant since at least 2005, when it appeared in The Pennsylvania Celebrities Cookbook beside his name — with no date, game, interview or publication attached. Quote Investigator ↗, which traced the saying in January 2024, concluded there is substantive evidence Bryant crafted it but found no direct citation to any speech, interview or article by him.

trail: 2005 — the earliest printing Quote Investigator documents ↗ is The Pennsylvania Celebrities Cookbook, page 16, where the line sits under “Kobe Bryant, Basketball Player, Philadelphia, PA” with no originating detail. The book was published by Stohn Books in 2005, as the editor’s own book page confirms ↗.

2007–2008 — the saying spreads through an email/Google Group list and then into newspapers on two continents: the Daily Dispatch of East London, South Africa in May 2008, and a student profile in the Modesto Bee in August 2008. Both credit Bryant; neither says when or where he said it (citations verified by QI ↗).

2009 — NBA centre Hasheem Thabeet posted a longer version of his own in March, and in July The Commercial Appeal of Memphis attributed a version of the saying to him. QI records that the line was already circulating under Bryant’s name (full chronology ↗).

Since 2010 — sports-quote anthologies and coaching books reprint it as Bryant’s, and quote databases carry it with no source at all. Wikiquote’s Bryant page ↗, which does cite his book, a 2019 interview and his 2016 farewell speech, does not list this line.
source.excerptNote: As printed on page 16 of the 2005 cookbook, in a chapter of tailgating recipes; Quote Investigator verified the page with scans. The book pairs recipes with one-line quotations from well-known Pennsylvanians, and offers no citation for any of them.

source.rightsNote: No public-domain claim is possible here. The originating work has never been identified, and the earliest documented printing is a 2005 book — well after the 1931 U.S. public-domain cutoff — so both the cookbook text and any remark Bryant himself made are modern, protected material rather than free text. Short attributed quotations of this length are conventionally reproduced with credit; nothing on this page should be read as clearing wider reuse.

author.heading: Who was Kobe Bryant?
author.metaLine: 1978–2020 · NBA guard · 20 seasons with the Los Angeles Lakers
author.bio: Kobe Bean Bryant was born 23 August 1978 in Philadelphia and played his entire NBA career — 20 seasons, 1996 to 2016 — with the Los Angeles Lakers, winning five championships. After retiring he won the Academy Award for Best Animated Short Film for Dear Basketball (2017). He died on 26 January 2020 in a helicopter crash in Calabasas, California. His self-styled “Mamba Mentality” made him one of the most quoted athletes alive — and, like every such figure, a magnet for lines nobody can source.

misattribution.heading: How the credit has drifted
misattribution.intro: Nobody has shown the line is not Bryant’s. But the way it travels — sourceless, occasionally re-credited, and with the wording quietly mutating — is worth seeing.

items.why: In March 2009 the basketball player posted an expanded version of his own, and by July 2009 The Commercial Appeal of Memphis was attributing a version of the saying to him. Quote Investigator notes the line was already in circulation under Bryant’s name before this — see the 2009 citations ↗.
Both AZQuotes ↗ and Goodreads ↗ print it as “Everyting negative” — the same typo copied from one database to the next, neither offering any source.
When Natalia Bryant’s graduation cap carried the line in 2021, Black Enterprise printed it with “pressures” in the plural, per Quote Investigator’s citation ↗.
Wikiquote’s Kobe Bryant page ↗ carries quotations tied to The Mamba Mentality, a 2019 interview and his 13 April 2016 farewell speech — but not this one.

misattribution.truthLine: The honest answer: Quote Investigator ↗ finds substantive evidence Bryant crafted the line, but no citation to a speech, interview or article by him — and the earliest printing on record is a 2005 cookbook that gives nothing but his name.

context.heading: Why this one is so hard to pin down
lead: This is one of the most reproduced sentences in the whole “Mamba Mentality” canon — posters, notebooks, locker-room walls, graduation caps. It also sounds exactly like Bryant, which is precisely what makes it slippery: the sentence became a slogan before anybody bothered to write down where it came from.

The documented trail does not start in an arena or a press conference. It starts in a Pennsylvania charity cookbook, where a one-line quotation sits under a recipe with nothing but a name and a hometown. Every later appearance — South African and Californian newspapers in 2008, sports-quote anthologies in 2010, his daughter Natalia’s graduation cap in 2021 — copies the attribution forward without ever adding a date or a venue.
detailsBody: A dated transcript, broadcast, or contemporaneous article in which Bryant says or writes the sentence — ideally before 2005, the year of the earliest printing on record. Quote Investigator explicitly invites future researchers to improve the evidence.

Absence of proof is not proof of fabrication. Nothing here suggests the line was invented for him; it simply has never been tied to a moment. Quotle.info records that gap rather than papering over it.
context.pull: Credited to Bryant since 2005 — and never once with a date, a venue, or a source.
